title: Research Associate (Technology & Content)
description: Position Snapshot Reports To Project Leader Duration 8 months Location Lucknow, with field travel to Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh Team Works within a 7-member core project team (Project Leader, 2 Research Associates, Special Educator, M&E and Data Officer, Field Coordinator, IT/AT Technician) Compensation Commensurate with qualifications and experience, as per SPARC India's project salary scale Nature of Role Full-time About SPARC India SPARC India (School for Potential Advancement and Restoration of Confidence) is a pioneering not-for-profit committed to the empowerment of marginalised populations, with a strong focus on Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). Founded in 1996 by Dr. Amitabh Mehrotra — himself a person with cerebral palsy and a nationally recognised disability-rights advocate — SPARC India has built a 30-year legacy of grassroots service delivery, policy advocacy, and systemic inclusion across Lucknow and Barabanki districts, Uttar Pradesh. About the Project SPARC India, in technical partnership with IIT Bombay and with support from Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), is implementing an 8-month technology- and AI-driven intervention to transform the learning experience of 50 children with disabilities (cerebral palsy, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, and sensory impairments) across Lucknow and Barabanki. The project delivers individualised assessment and AT/AI device matching, two technology-enabled inclusive classrooms, and capacity building of 15 educators, therapists, and caregivers, with structured family and community engagement. Purpose of the Position The Research Associate (Technology & Content) leads the project's assistive-technology (AT) and AI needs assessment, device specification, and accessible digital-content development. Working directly with IIT Bombay's technical team, the role translates each child's assessed needs into concrete, well-specified technology deployments, two functioning smart classrooms, and a growing library of 80+ accessible learning resources. Key Responsibilities 1. Assistive Technology & AI Needs Assessment • Conduct individualised AT and AI needs assessments for 50 children, in coordination with the Research Associate (Assessment & Evaluation), the therapy team, and IIT Bombay's technical team. • Translate clinical/functional assessment findings into specific device and software recommendations — e.g. communication boards/AAC apps, adapted seating, hearing aids, screen readers, and AI-based learning tools. • Finalise device and AI-tool specifications and support vendor identification, comparison, and negotiation ahead of lump-sum procurement (Months 5–6). • Conduct technology audits and device-utilisation reviews after deployment to verify appropriateness, uptake, and impact. 2. Accessible Content & Digital Repository • Lead development of 80+ accessible learning resources — adapted worksheets, AAC-compatible materials, screen-reader-friendly digital content, and AI-assisted learning aids — mapped to each child's IEP and curriculum needs. • Build and maintain a digital repository/resource library for use by educators, therapists, and families, ensuring content is organised, version-controlled, and easily retrievable. • Pilot and iterate content based on classroom feedback and digital-usage analytics. 3. Smart Classroom & Technology Deployment • Support the design and technical set-up of two technology-enabled inclusive (“smart”) classrooms — hardware, internet connectivity, displays, sensory zones, and accessible workstations. • Coordinate with the IT/AT Technician on installation, configuration, and AMC (annual maintenance contract) arrangements for devices and classroom technology. • Review weekly digital device-usage analytics (with the M&E and Data Officer) to monitor adoption and flag under-utilised devices or tools. 4. Training & Capacity-Building Support • Co-design and co-deliver technical training modules for 15 professionals (educators, therapists, facilitators) on AT and AI integration, as part of the project's Training-of-Trainers (ToT) model. • Support family-orientation sessions on using assistive devices and digital tools at home. • Provide on-demand technical troubleshooting guidance to teachers and families during pilot deployment. 5. Coordination & Documentation • Serve as the primary technical liaison with IIT Bombay on AT/AI assessment methodology, tool selection, and device specifications. • Contribute technology-related sections to milestone reports, the midline/endline evaluations, and the joint research paper with IIT Bombay. • Maintain documentation of device specifications, procurement rationale, and utilisation data to support FCRA-compliant financial and narrative reporting. Key Deliverables • AT/AI needs-assessment report (Month 2). • Finalised device and AI-tool specifications (Month 4). • Two operational smart classrooms (Month 6). • 80+ accessible learning resources and a functioning digital repository (phased, by Month 8). • Technology-audit and device-utilisation reports. Qualifications & Experience • Essential: Master's degree (MA/M.Tech) in Assistive Technology, Educational Technology, Computer Science, or a related field. • Experience: 2–3 years working with assistive technology, EdTech content development, or inclusive digital design. Candidates with a strong project/technical portfolio and relevant Master's may also be considered. • Technical skills: familiarity with AAC tools, screen readers, adaptive hardware, basic AI/ML-enabled learning tools, and content-authoring or digital-repository platforms. • Sector knowledge: understanding of accessibility standards (WCAG), Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and disability-inclusive EdTech practice. Key Competencies • Strong technical problem-solving ability combined with an instructional-design sensibility. • Comfort working hands-on with hardware/software in a classroom setting, alongside non-technical colleagues and families. • Creativity in adapting content for diverse disability profiles. • Ability to work to milestone deadlines and coordinate closely with an external technical partner (IIT Bombay). How to apply Interested candidates may send an updated CV along with a cover letter outlining relevant experience to SPARC India's recruitment team, indicating the position title in the subject line. Shortlisted candidates will be invited for a written assessment and interview. Organization: SPARC India Website: www.sparcindia.in Locations: Lucknow & Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh E-Mail: admin@sparcindia.in

title: Program Director – Public Health Outreach
description: Designation Program Director – Public Health Outreach Location: Ranchi (Jharkhand) / Bhubaneswar (Odisha) / Raipur (Chhattisgarh) / Guwahati (Assam) No. of Vacancies: 4 Project/Unit: Global Alliance for Viksit Bharat (GAVB) Project Background The Global Alliance for Viksit Bharat (GAVB) is a landmark social development initiative designed to uplift 200 million Indians living in multidimensional poverty. With a transformative investment, GAVB concentrates efforts on five priority states—Jharkhand, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Bihar (JACOB states)—which are disproportionately impacted by acute poverty. Health and Education account for 67% of the Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MDPI). GAVB works closely with state governments to strengthen public health systems, improve service delivery, and enhance community wellbeing. The Communicable Disease (CD) portfolio specifically addresses Tuberculosis (TB) and Malaria—two diseases that disproportionately affect vulnerable populations including tribal communities, urban poor, and migrant workers. GAVB's approach leverages Digitization, Decentralization, Leadership & Institutions, and Inclusion to enhance health service delivery. Domain expertise with proven solutions lays the foundation for introduction, progression, and gradual integration of innovations into government public health systems. Job Summary The Program Director - Public Health Outreach, reporting to the Core Team Member, will serve as the state’s anchor for driving population-level health outcomes through last-mile system transformation, with a focus on improving coverage, quality, and equity of primary healthcare services. The role will be accountable for translating GAVB’s vision into scalable, state-owned outreach models that strengthen demand generation, early risk identification, and service utilization across RMNCH continuums - particularly for vulnerable and underserved populations. The Program Director will provide strategic leadership to the Directorate of Health (DoH) and State Health Society (SHS)/National Health Mission (NHM) in designing and implementing comprehensive public health programs, with a strong focus on preventive, promotive and primary healthcare. This includes strengthening frontline systems by enhancing the capacities of community health workers (ASHAs, ANMs, CHOs), enhancing supervisory support mechanisms, improving last-mile service delivery through outreach service delivery platforms and engaging effective community systems. The role will also focus on improving coverage, equity, and quality of outreach services, particularly for vulnerable and underserved populations in the state. Additionally, the Program Director will be accountable for end-to-end strategy development and execution for public health and outreach initiatives, ensuring high-quality program delivery, scalable models and measurable impact. The role will provide strong leadership, direction, and oversight to teams, enabling effective implementation and sustained improvements in public health outcomes at scale. Key Responsibilities 1. Technical Leadership and Strategy Development Serve as a thought partner to state leadership (Mission Director, DHS, DoH, NHM) on primary healthcare transformation. Support the development and operationalization of state and national-level strategies for community-based healthcare aligned with national guidelines and state priorities. Identify systemic gaps in outreach service delivery, community engagement and last-mile service coverage and initiate innovative and scalable solutions. Strengthen convergence across departments (ICDS, PRI, etc.) to enhance effectiveness of outreach platforms. Anchor cross-portfolio convergence within GAVB (medical services, data systems, HRH). 2. Program Implementation Support the implementation and scale-up of high-impact outreach interventions at VHSNDs and HWCs, ensuring delivery of RMNCH and NCD services and health promotion activities. Strengthen the execution and governance of VHSNDs to ensure quality service delivery for antenatal care and timely identification of maternal complication, identification and prevention of childhood diseases and promoting healthy spacing options to couples. Enhance functionality of HWCs including preventive, promotive and referral services. Improve last-mile delivery of services through better microplanning, supportive supervision, and use of community-level data. Strengthen supply chain mechanisms to ensure uninterrupted availability of essential drugs, diagnostics, and logistics at outreach points. Strengthen referral linkages between community platforms and higher-level health facilities. 3. Community Engagement and Institutional Strengthening Leverage community platforms (VHSNCs, SHGs, PRI) as accountability and demand-generation engines, not just awareness forums. Design and institutionalize behavior change strategies linked to measurable service uptake. Facilitate capacity building of VHSNC and JAS members on planning, monitoring and utilization of funds for local health actions. Enhance awareness generation and behavior change communication (BCC) strategies to improve health-seeking behaviors at household level. 4. Capacity Building Support the design and delivery of capacity building programs for frontline workers (ASHAs, ANMs, CHOs) on screening, mobilization, outreach service delivery and referrals. Strengthen institutional capacity of training bodies such as SIHFW and related institutions for sustained capacity building of outreach cadres including FLWs and their supervisors. Institutionalize mentoring and supportive supervision mechanisms for continuous skill enhancement of frontline workers. Build capacities of block and district officials for planning, supervision and improving outreach services. 5. Monitoring, Evaluation and Digital Strengthening Support the development and implementation of monitoring frameworks for VHSND and HWC performance indicators and health outcomes at household level. Enable beneficiary-level tracking systems integrating multiple data sources (RCH, HMIS, ICDS, etc.). Promote the use of digital tools and platforms for real-time tracking of service delivery, beneficiary coverage and health outcomes. Facilitate regular data review and use for decision-making at block, district and state levels using digital tools. Support documentation of best practices, case studies and innovations in outreach and community engagement. 6. Policy Influence and Stakeholder Engagement Support the Directorate and State Health Society/National Health Mission in formulating policies, guidelines and operational frameworks for strengthening outreach and community processes. Ensure all outreach models are embedded within government systems, with clear ownership, budget lines, and review mechanisms. Engage with partners, donors and civil society organizations to align outreach efforts with broader health system goals. Influence for increased investments in primary healthcare, community processes and outreach platforms. Essential Qualification & Experience MBA/ Masters in Social Work/Public Health/Rural Management/Hospital Management/PGDM from Tier-1 institutions (IIMs/IITs/MDI etc.). Minimum 10 years of experience in public health, preferably community health and outreach health service delivery or development setting.
